description: Found while costing fz-sc8.14: String.duplicate("ab", 80000) aborts with 'thread main has overflowed its stack' on fz2 run (ad21e1635). lib/string.fz writes duplicate(s, n) as s <> duplicate(s, n - 1), which is not tail recursive. Elixir's duplicate/2 is :binary.copy/2. Write it so its depth does not grow with n (an accumulator, or doubling), and test it at a count well past the old overflow point on interp, run and build. Its cost then depends on the binary append fix in the ticket 'Walking or building a binary costs time linear in its length'.
title: String.duplicate/2 does not overflow the stack for large counts
